newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zaire exiles back rebels, oppose intervention.
newsitem.headline: Zaire exiles back rebels, oppose intervention.

text.p: A coalition of Zairean exile groups in Switzerland on Tuesday voiced support for rebels now in control of much of the east of the country and said they offered hope for an end to dictatorship and oppression.

In a statement issued in Geneva, the coalition also accused France of campaigning for an international force to stop the fighting in order to rescue the administration of long-time President Mobutu Sese Seko from collapse.

"The Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire is a democratic movement open to all and determined to liberate our entire people," declared the statement, issued in the name of some 3,000 Swiss-based Zaireans.

"The eternal despoilers of the Congo have already realised this. That is why they are determined to block and destroy (the Alliance's) action. We must join efforts to stop France's demagogy and machiavellianism," it said.
"Mobutu and his companions are criminals," the statement said. "Let us line up behind the army of liberation to put a final end to more than 30 years of systematic robbery and degradation," it added.

One of the statement's authors, Mubengay Bafwa, who is president of a Forum of Zairean Patriots in Switzerland, told Reuters the Alliance, led by former Marxist Laurent Kabila, had support from people all over Zaire.
"This is a movement of all those who want to end the bloody dictatorship of Mobutu," he said. "It is backed by people from many tribes and of many political tendencies."

France's President Jacques Chirac -- in an appeal echoed by United Nations Secretary-General Koffi Annan -- has called on the international community to force a ceasefire in Zaire and try to protect Rwandan Hutu refugees fleeing from the rebels.

The Hutus, variously estimated at between 150,000 and 350,000, left their own country after the 1994 massacres of hundreds of thousands of Tutsis, fearing reprisals by the Tutsi-led Rwandan Patriotic Front which came to power in the wake of the genocide.

Kabila's forces were at first made up mainly of Zairean Tutsis, who began fighting last year after Zaire's army -- with support from remnants of the army of the former Rwandan Hutu government -- moved to expel them from the country.
